package.description: Manage SQL, NoSQL and analytical databases in one app

en-US.description: Manage SQL, NoSQL and analytical databases in one app
en-US.longDescription:
DBine is a desktop database manager for relational, analytical, document, key-value, graph, time-series and search databases. One workbench connects to PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, Oracle, MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra, ClickHouse, DuckDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, Elasticsearch, Neo4j, InfluxDB and many more engines.

Explore and query:
- A tree per connection and database, with saved queries kept inside each database
- A SQL editor with each engine's dialect, completion of tables and columns, and script execution
- A fast results grid with cell editing, filters, sorting, charts and a JSON tree view
- Graphical execution plans, a visual query builder and query optimization hints
- Search across object names, columns and stored code, and run code on several databases at once

Design and move data:
- Table designer, ER diagrams and script generation
- Compare schemas and data, then migrate, clone or sync databases between engines
- Import CSV, JSON, XLSX and XML; export results in many formats; generate test data and data subsets
- Rename objects with an impact analysis of everything that depends on them

Administer:
- Server monitor, live processes and a profiler of the queries clients run
- Users and permissions, backups, health checks and database properties
- SSH tunnels, including chains of bastions and the SSH agent
- Read-only connections and production safeguards

Assistant and integrations:
- An AI assistant that writes and explains queries with a local built-in model or Ollama; it never runs anything by itself
- A local MCP server so AI coding assistants can work with your connections, with every write approved in DBine
- End-to-end encrypted cloud sync of connections, queries and settings to your own account
- A script library and projects backed by git

Passwords are stored encrypted with a key kept in the system keychain, and never go into the state file or the logs.
en-US.name: DBine
